Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Highlights

There were no new releases in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker is highly active with a large batch of desktop-app regressions being closed as duplicates — most notably the missing Routines sidebar, the usage-ring context window regression, and the dead-key input bug on Windows. A consistent theme in today's activity is that several distinct reports are converging on the same underlying defects (Routines sidebar, prompt suggestions, context popover, MCP scope handling), suggesting maintainers are consolidating duplicates ahead of a fix. On the PR side, triage/dedupe automation is being moved to Claude Sonnet 5.5, while a backlog of documentation and plugin fixes from external contributor nielskaspers closes out.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. (Omit.)

3. Hot Issues

  1. #102247 [CLOSED] Routines sidebar section hidden after update — link Windows desktop regression where scheduled Routines vanish from the sidebar and run sessions become unreachable. 8 comments, 5 👍; closed as duplicate, indicating widespread impact across the 2.37337.1 build.

  2. #102185 [CLOSED] Prompt suggestions no longer appear (Windows) — link The composer stuck showing "Enter to send, Ctrl+Enter to queue" with no suggested prompts. 6 👍, closed as bug — a UX regression affecting everyday Code-tab flow.

  3. #101012 [OPEN] Windows TaskStop leaves orphaned Git Bash child processes — link Background-task kill doesn't reap grep/find/du/sleep children, which linger for hours. Still open with a repro — a genuine resource-leak hazard for Windows users.

  4. #104833 [CLOSED] MCP servers from project/local scope removed on 2nd message — link MCP servers silently drop after the first message in sessions launched from pre-warmed "spare" instances. 5 👍, closed — significant reliability concern for MCP-dependent workflows.

  5. #78439 [OPEN] Backup retention evicts last good .claude.json after corruption — link keep-last-5 counts corrupted backups toward the cap, making config loss permanent. Open, data-loss severity, still unresolved since July.

  6. #105498 [CLOSED] Desktop silently deletes transcripts after 30 days despite "Never" setting — link Sessions older than ~30 days open empty and are marked transcriptUnavailable. Closed as duplicate — data-loss with strong community concern.

  7. #80902 [OPEN] Subagents default to claude-fable-5 while session is Opus — link Silent, more-expensive default that ignores the session model and any config. Open since July, low vote count but notable cost impact.

  8. #105881 [OPEN] Session paused by Opus 5.5 cyber safeguard during legitimate security work — link Over-broad safeguard flagging non-cyber work, interrupting legitimate security tasks. Open — a recurring friction point with newer model safeguards.

  9. #91779 [CLOSED] CoworkVMService fails crash-recovery config, blocks Desktop startup — link "Access is denied" leaves the service down until a full reboot. Closed as duplicate alongside #89711/#85840 — a cluster of Windows service-install defects.

  10. #103814 [CLOSED] Plugin Button presses refused (ui_press handled:false) — link Button handles held per-site and renumbered on props change, breaking multi-client interaction. Closed as duplicate — an architecture-level plugin API issue.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #106583 Move issue triage and dedupe workflows to Sonnet 5.5 — link Migrates claude-issue-triage.yml, claude-dedupe-issues.yml, and claude.yml to the 5.5 family — directly relevant given today's heavy dedup activity.

  2. #19866 fix(ralph-wiggum): handle empty PROMPT_PARTS with set -u — link Fixes a crash when running /ralph-loop without arguments.

  3. #19867 fix(code-review): allow re-reviews when new commits are pushed — link Adds smarter skip logic and a --force flag for the code-review plugin.

  4. #24360 docs: add configuration file reference to README — link Documents the ~/.claude.json vs ~/.claude/settings.json scope/precedence distinction.

  5. #40822 docs(vscode): add "Not responding" status bar guidance — link Clarifies the ~60s no-response warning state versus normal spinner progress.

  6. #44071 docs: capitalize 'Get Started' heading — link Trivial README heading consistency fix.

  7. #50672 docs(changelog): fix skill name in 2.1.111 entry — link Corrects /less-permission-prompts → /fewer-permission-prompts.

(Only 7 PRs were updated in the window; all are listed above.)

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided. (Omit.)

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session/archive management: Multiple requests (#104573, #104004, #105723) ask for a sidebar toggle to view archived sessions and per-machine (non-synced) sidebar group/sort settings.
  • Desktop UX toggles: Suppressing the clipboard-change warning toast (#89559) and restoring the context-window line in the usage popover (#102615, #102204).
  • Account/auth flexibility: Allowing users to change the email on an existing account (#103389, follow-up to #61022).
  • Remote Control resilience: Requests to keep Remote Control alive across silent auto-updates (#105671, #105926).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent auto-updates disrupt work: Two separate reports (#105671, #105926) describe background updates stopping all local sessions and leaving Remote Control down, stranding remote users.
  • Data loss & config corruption: Corrupted-backup eviction (#78439) and transcript deletion despite "Never" (#105498) are high-severity recurring complaints.
  • Windows desktop instability: A large share of today's issues are Windows-specific desktop regressions — Routines sidebar (#102247, #104237), prompt suggestions (#102185, #103159), dead keys (#106555, #106602), and CoworkVMService failures (#89711, #91779).
  • MCP scope/reliability: MCP servers dropping mid-session (#104833) erodes trust in project/local MCP configs.
  • Model/safeguard friction: Subagents silently using an unexpected model (#80902) and over-broad Opus 5.5 safeguards pausing legitimate work (#105881).

Note: No GitHub Discussions data was supplied; Section 5 is omitted per instructions. PR "Comments" fields were undefined in the source data.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Highlights

Two new alpha builds shipped (rust-v0.167.0-alpha.2 and .3) with no public changelog, while a large batch of PRs landed focused on TUI telemetry, session management, and pausing Bazel-based release artifacts after a revoked BuildBuddy key. The community's attention is overwhelmingly on rate limits: more than half of the top 30 issues ask for auto-resume after quota resets, and two new threads push back hard on the reported plan to merge ChatGPT and Codex quotas in December. Cross-device and attachment handling also surfaced several fresh bugs (XLSX/PPTX send spinning, stale approval modals).

2. Releases

  • rust-v0.167.0-alpha.3 — 0.167.0-alpha.3 (no release notes) — Release
  • rust-v0.167.0-alpha.2 — 0.167.0-alpha.2 (no release notes) — Release

Both are pre-release alpha cuts; the only substantive signal is PR #58757, which removes Bazel outputs from DotSlash configs because they are absent from the Cargo-only release asset fixture for 0.167.0-alpha.2.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #21073 — Auto-resume CLI session when usage limit resets (23 comments, 👍89) — The single most-upvoted open request: when Codex hits a quota mid-task and reports the reset time, the session should resume automatically instead of waiting for a human. Link
  2. #57721 — macOS: mobile-created remote chats report browser disabled (17 comments) — Remote chats created entirely from Android cannot access the connected Mac until a desktop message "initializes" the thread. High impact for remote/mobile workflows. Link
  3. #53042 — macOS Quick Chat no longer launches (15 comments, 👍24) — Quick Chat and its native window service are absent in build 26.1007.30912; a regression in a frequently used entry point. Link
  4. #28931 — Auto-resume /Goal after 5h limit reset (15 comments, 👍76) — The App-side twin of #21073; strong consensus that paused Goals should resume once quota refreshes. Link
  5. #45873 — ChatGPT Desktop personalization shows Codex settings (14 comments) — A UI/settings bleed between the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex, confusing Plus users. Link
  6. #56941 — Windows UI lag persists after Computer Use (13 comments) — System-wide sluggishness that only resolves when codex-computer-use.exe is killed; a serious performance/cleanup bug on Windows. Link

  • Tool-scoping intelligence: smarter tool selection under the 400-error threshold (#24246), proactive skill/subagent invocation (#21968).
  • Timeouts and guardrails: per-tool-call timeouts (#27423), configurable model request timeouts (#30082).
  • Observability & debuggability: subagent trajectories in /chat share (#22598), subagent context in bug reports (#21763), terminal session status (#29918).

  1. Subagent delegation is unreliable. The generalist agent hangs indefinitely (#21409, 👍8) and subagents misreport forced termination as success (#22323, #21983). Users are disabling delegation as a workaround — a direct hit to the multi-agent value proposition.

  2. The Browser Agent is the weakest link. Ignored settings (#22267), fail-fast lock handling (#22232), and Wayland breakage (#21983) combine into a subsystem that Linux users struggle to use at all.

  3. Configuration silently doesn't apply. settings.json overrides (#22267), symlinked agents (#20079), and missing subagent context in bug reports (#21763) all erode trust in the tooling surface.

  • Durable/embedded runtime controls — Conversation deletion (#11026), context handoff (#11557), host-provided Code Mode output writers (#11070), and robust behavior under Durable Objects / SQLite (#11669, #11661).
  • Context/compaction correctness — Interleaved compaction (#8301), overflow detection from llama.cpp (#10885), and accurate getContextUsage() (#10287).
  • Network/proxy & auth hardening — Proxy-aware OAuth (#11666), symlink-safe refresh locking (#11655), Bedrock client reuse (#11527).
  • Provider coverage — Adding glm-5.3 (#11658) and general allowlist vs. models.dev reconciliation.
  • Editor/TUI QoL — /new [prompt...] (#11664), Shift+Enter in legacy terminals (#4037), overlay behavior with images (#11584).
  • Extensibility — user_bash recordedCommand (#11665), native messaging extensions (#11668).
  • GUI aspirations — Recurring community request for a friendlier GUI (#11653).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Provider-specific surprises: Bedrock creating a client per request (#11527); Anthropic/OpenAI reset semantics with ChatGPT Pro (#10480).
  • Silent/incorrect failure detection: llama.cpp overflow unhandled (#10885); false "timed out" from bash (#11613).
  • State/lock races: symlinked auth.json bypasses refresh lock (#11655); lazyApi first-load promise leaking across Durable Object contexts (#11661).
  • Storage brittleness: JSON depth limits on SQLite (#11669); no delete primitive in durable storage (#11026).
  • SDK/prototype fragility: wrapUIPromptContext spreads prototypes away (#8829); codemode name collision on tools (#11226).
  • Documentation gaps: settings audit shows several keys have no UI path (#11663, #11662).

Generated from github.com/earendil-works/pi data captured 2026-11-02. Stats: 0 releases · 25 issues updated · 3 PRs updated · 2 discussions updated.

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Highlights

The Qwen Code project shipped v0.26.5 across three artifacts (CLI, nightly, and Desktop), headlined by bounded SQL history queries for Managed sessions — a notable step toward paged, resource-bounded session retrieval. However, the release is partially broken: the sandbox image for 0.26.5 failed to publish, which cascades into failures across all sandbox-based CI lanes. Meanwhile, CI infrastructure instability remains the dominant theme of the day, with recurring disk exhaustion, missing Node.js on pool hosts, and flaky Managed Agent fault gates occupying the top of both the issue and PR queues.

2. Releases

v0.26.5 / desktop-v0.26.5 / v0.26.5-nightly.20261101

  • Bounded SQL history queries (PR #15839) — Managed local H2 and Hosted MySQL now support paged recent-message and journal-transaction queries, replacing unbounded history reads. This is the release's flagship change and directly addresses long-session memory and latency concerns.
  • Session event delivery loop refactor (PR #15952) — deduplicates the loop shared between managed-agent event paths.
  • Generated UI: continued card-based chat interaction support.

⚠️ Release caveat: Issue #16039 reports that ghcr.io/qwenlm/qwen-code:0.26.5 was never published — the release build job failed before the image push. Every sandbox-based lane (/resolve, sandboxed review, autofix) currently crashes with manifest unknown when installing the matching npm version. Expect a hotfix or re-run.

No breaking changes are declared.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate (147 comments). The single most active thread in the tracker. A required check is red on main for an unidentified test, meaning every full-tier PR is blocked. The comment count (6+ weeks of updates) signals a persistent infra problem rather than a code defect.

  2. #16039 — Sandbox image for 0.26.5 not published. Directly impacts release usability; auto-filed by the release bot. High urgency because it blocks the sandboxed review and autofix tooling the project itself relies on.

  3. #15898 — Hosted process fault gates fail on main; postFailureLoads varies run to run. A textbook flaky test: two separate main runs fail the same job with different measurements. Now closed, but it exemplifies the non-determinism problem in the Managed Agent test suite.

  4. #9005 — Anthropic wire missing stream-safety protections the OpenAI wire has. A long-running (since August) P1 correctness gap: streaming cancellation and safety handling are asymmetric between providers. Companion to PR #16079.

  5. #13570 — Auto mode blocks inert text mentioning the amend phrase. A permissions false-positive: the guard pattern-matches raw command text rather than parsed invocations, so documentation or comments mentioning git commit --amend are blocked ahead of the user's own rules. Addressed by PR #16075.

  6. #15933 — Desktop update from pre-fix Windows build still fails. Users on older desktop builds cannot upgrade past node.exe file-lock errors because the old binary drives the update. A self-reinforcing upgrade trap for a subset of Windows users.

  7. #16030 — Linux AppImage missing 9 WebKitGTK libraries. The only non-Debian Linux artifact ships broken image paste. Users on rpm distros must manually patch library holes — a packaging completeness problem with an easy-to-verify repro.

  8. #16005 — ecs-qwen-hz6-18 has no Node.js on PATH. Because Lint & Static is a required check, any commit routed to this pool host goes red for reasons unrelated to code. A concrete, actionable fleet-configuration bug.

  9. #16003 — CI runners run out of disk; RocketMQ refuses writes, Java lanes can't create temp dirs. Disk exhaustion recurs across multiple runs and pools, and is invisible in failure summaries. Points to a systemic capacity issue rather than a one-off.

  10. #15894 — A stop sent as a user message doesn't cancel a pending loop_wakeup. In self-paced /loop mode, an explicit user stop fails to cancel a scheduled wakeup, so the loop re-arms itself. A genuine behavioral bug in the background-automation roadmap with a clear reproduction.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16075 — fix(permissions): match amend invocations instead of raw text. The proper fix for #13570: parses compound commands, strips heredocs, unwraps shell wrappers, and only then checks for git commit invocations. A model example of moving from regex guarding to structured parsing.

  2. #16082 — fix(web-shell): surface Managed session list failures. Replaces a raw error sentence at the top of the pane with a localized, retryable load-error notice carrying HTTP status, error code, and request ID. Fixes the UX complaint in #14918.

  3. #16079 — fix(core): surface Anthropic refusal details. Carries refusal metadata through the finish event as a category-specific user message, improving on the generic SAFETY notice. Complements the streaming-safety work tracked in #9005.

  4. #14953 — fix(core): keep compression requests within the context window. Compression now respects an admission check and retries with a size derived from the rejection. Directly relevant to the context-performance roadmap.

  5. #16068 — fix(ci): fail Java lanes before disk exhaustion. Adds a disk-floor preflight to all six routable Java lanes, checking both workspace and runner temp filesystems. A pragmatic mitigation for #16003.

  6. #15634 — feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn. Adds a fourth dispatchMode (inject) so messages arriving mid-turn reach the agent at its next tool-batch boundary instead of being buffered. Important for interactive multi-channel agents.

  7. #14748 — fix(cli): gate project hooks behind an approval dialog. Brings workspace-declared hooks under the same approval model as project MCP servers, showing event, matcher, and command before load. A meaningful supply-chain hardening step.

  8. #15928 — feat(web-shell): host mount entries + managed empty-state layout. Adds renderManagedAgentWebShell so non-React hosts can embed the WebShell without hand-drawing chrome, with no hardcoded backend address.

  9. #15466 — feat(serve): user-scope Skill activation routes. Adds PUT /skills/:name/activation and batch activation (up to 100 names) at user scope. Fills a gap alongside the existing extensions activation API.

  10. #15635 — feat(qqbot): deliver proactive loop messages as active group messages. Makes QQ the fifth adapter to opt into proactive delivery, enabling loop firings and background-task results to reach group chats outside the reply window.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the issue and PR backlog, the most-requested directions are:

  • Managed Agent observability and boundedness — bounded SQL history queries (#15839), paged session metadata, failure surfacing in Web Shell (#14918/#16082), and disabling the models.dev catalog refresh for privacy (#16006). Users want Managed Agent state to be inspectable, paginated, and optionally offline.
  • Settings and configuration control — privacy opt-outs (#16006), user-scope Skill activation (#15466), and per-channel forwarding options (#15904). The theme is giving operators fine-grained, settings-level control over what the agent does automatically.
  • Context/memory efficiency — compression within the context window (#14953), deduplicating auto-recall hook context against local memory (#14089), and matching memory-index advice to budget (#15368). All target the context-performance roadmap.
  • Cross-provider correctness parity — stream-safety and refusal-detail handling on the Anthropic wire (#9005, #16079). As multi-provider support matures, users expect feature parity, not just connectivity.
  • Channel breadth and proactive delivery — QQ, Weixin, and other adapters gaining proactive/injected message delivery (#15634, #15635, #9307). The direction is toward always-on, multi-channel agents.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI instability is the #1 daily frustration. At least eight of the top issues today concern CI: flaky fault gates (#15898), missing Node.js on pool hosts (#16005), disk exhaustion (#16003), unpublished sandbox images (#16039), and routing requests for dedicated/self-hosted pools (#15461, #15967, #15968). Because several are required checks, this blocks unrelated PRs and erodes trust in green builds.
  • Self-inflicted release breakage — the 0.26.5 sandbox image failure (#16039) shows the release pipeline can publish npm artifacts whose matching container image is missing, leaving downstream tooling in a broken state.
  • Upgrade traps on Windows and Linux — the Windows desktop update lock (#15933) and the AppImage library hole (#16030) both leave users on older, vulnerable builds with no clean path forward.
  • False-positive permission guards — #13570 shows the cost of pattern-matching raw command text: inert documentation gets blocked, and users have no escape hatch. The fix (#16075) is welcome but highlights a broader "guard by parsing, not by regex" lesson.
  • Non-deterministic tests undermine confidence — flaky fault gates that "vary run to run" (#15898) and intermittent failures make it hard to distinguish real regressions from noise, slowing every review cycle.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-02

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-02 00:34 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw shows sustained high-velocity activity: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24h, split nearly evenly between open and closed states (271 open / 229 closed issues; 280 open / 220 merged-or-closed PRs). No new releases shipped today, so the bulk of activity is maintenance, review, and triage work. However, the issue tracker is dominated by stale-tagged, P1/P2 items — many carrying P0 "diamond lobster" ratings with clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr — indicating a growing gap between reported defects and fixes landing on main. Several long-running regressions (gateway event-loop blocking, memory provenance exclusion, plugin migration convergence) remain unresolved while UI/phone-width and Slack/multiline polish PRs move toward merge. Overall health is active but backlog-stressed: strong contributor throughput, weak closure rate on high-severity bugs.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. Latest known shipping point referenced in the data is 2026.10.8 (issue #187900), with users still on 2026.9.x reporting regressions introduced as far back as 2026.9.3–2026.9.7.

3. Project Progress

Notable PRs merged/closed (or advanced) today:

  • PR #190730 [CLOSED] — fix: preserve multiline Slack, Feishu, and Zalo command arguments — supersedes #185267 and closes #185266. Multiline /btw and /loop payloads now reach command dispatch intact. Link
  • PR #185267 [CLOSED] — Prior attempt at the same multiline-command fix across Slack/Feishu/Zalo. Link
  • PR #190196 [CLOSED] — fix(voice-call): preserve spaces after Unicode transcript overlaps — fixes the Meet in İstanbultomorrow concatenation bug in realtime voice. Link
  • PR #188633 [CLOSED] — fix(macos): screen.record reports requested instead of recorded duration/fps — closes #187604; recording metadata now reflects actual output. Link
  • PR #190643 [CLOSED] — fix(codex): retain compatible tool catalogs on settled local threads — resolves conversation loss after compatible tool additions. Link
  • PR #185434 [CLOSED] — fix(exec): macOS app node exec with timeoutSeconds 0 ends after 20 seconds — long-standing timeoutSeconds: 0 regression on macOS nodes. Link
  • PR #190725 [CLOSED] — chore(matrix): trim unused send fixtures and assertions — test hygiene only. Link

Advancing toward merge (open, ready-for-maintainer-look): #190727 (cron failure observations for plugins), #190318 (outbound delivered-receipt retention after heartbeat renewal failure), #190721 (memory forget --json honesty), #180212 (watchdog cause preservation in automation failures).

4. Community Hot Topics

Top discussions by comment count:

Item Title Comments Link
#160959 P0: Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) 69 Link
#42475 Feature: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at gateway (CLOSED) 29 Link
#53408 Bug: write/exec parameters silently dropped after long conversations 16 Link
#153426 P0: Curated memory roots silently excluded from bootstrap injection by provenance ratchet 16 Link
#144502 WhatsApp mobile can't play TTS voice notes (CLOSED) 15 Link
#143632 iMessage inbound messages re-delivered 2–3× (CLOSED) 15 Link

Underlying needs analysis: The dominant clustering is around reliability and observability of the agent runtime:

  1. Performance/crash-loop regressions from recent feature work (#160959, #167557) — the plugin-generation capture feature shipped in 2026.9.6 appears to have introduced process-blocking behavior at startup and re-publish.
  2. Memory subsystem trust — two independent reports (#153426, #137613, #138561) describe silent memory loss: curated MEMORY.md/USER.md being dropped from bootstrap, and pre-compaction flush gated off on CLI backends. Users have no diagnostics or recovery path.
  3. Cost governance — #42475 (per-agent budgets), though closed, accumulated significant interest, suggesting operators want gateway-level spend guardrails.
  4. Message integrity — #53408 and #143632 both involve silent parameter/duplicate-message failures where the UI shows nothing wrong.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity from today's updates:

P0 / Crash-Loop / Release-Blocker

  • #160959 — Gateway event-loop blocks for minutes when capturing large external plugin dependency trees (regression from #144252, shipped 2026.9.6). 69 comments, clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, impact:crash-loop. No fix PR. Link
  • #153426 — MEMORY.md/USER.md permanently and silently excluded from bootstrap injection once provenance originClass flips to "untrusted" — triggerable by ordinary web-search turns. No CLI, no diagnostics, no recovery. impact:ux-release-blocker. Link

P1

  • #187900 — openclaw doctor hangs indefinitely at startup title frame on Linux (all modes, PTY and non-interactive). impact:crash-loop. Link
  • #167557 — Deferred plugin data/settings migration never converges on Linux/npm; "managed handoff lease database identity changed". Link
  • #167876 — Talk consultations lose caller authority after session setup. impact:security. Link
  • #156895 — Agent-created automation jobs fail closed in ~20ms with "Scheduled account is unavailable" despite being configured. impact:security. Link
  • #138272 — Android Talk (gateway-relay) drops with "no live response owner" on task-requiring turns; confirmed across 3 versions. Link
  • #144336 — Deferred config-reload restart (SIGUSR1) fails its shutdown step. Link
  • #128140 — memory_search tool always times out (15s) while CLI openclaw memory search works. Link
  • #128067 — Beta.7 field report: 6 reliability defect classes (persistence, delivery, restart-recovery). Link
  • #137710 — Native Codex completion recorded but does not wake sessions_yield parent. clawsweeper:linked-pr-open. Link
  • #140455 — @openclaw/google-meet 2026.9.2 agent voice broken on current Meet (circular-JSON crash). Link

P2 / Notable

  • #53408 — write/exec tool parameters silently dropped after 15+ turns (2 👍). Link
  • #164394 — Control UI WebChat transcript micro-jitter. Link
  • #173058 — Security: tools.fs.workspaceOnly doesn't restrict file tools — agent runtime also gets OpenClaw state root as allowed working dir. Link
  • #154474 — Completion batch republished ~15× to top-level session; operator stop dropped mid-loop. Link
  • #141172 — agent.run.started leaked forever when a run dies before first session commit; FK failure + appendTranscriptEventSync throws. Link
  • #131150 — Slack DMs silently dropped for all accounts after gateway restart with multi-account socket mode. Link
  • #114913 — Memory search: bound primary embeddings before outer tool deadline and fall back to FTS. Link

Fix PR status: Most P0/P1 items carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr — i.e., no fix PR exists, only #137710 has a linked open PR. This is the single most important health signal in today's data.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

High-signal feature requests updated today:

  • #67413 — Per-agent dreaming configuration (5 👍) — currently memory-core dreaming runs on all workspaces simultaneously, causing memory spikes and OOM kills. Strong candidate for next minor. Link
  • #138366 — Let memory slot owner drive the Dreams page (dreaming provider in MemoryPluginCapability). Link
  • #128090 — Rendered Markdown preview in Review files (4 👍). Link
  • #91676 — Opt-in skills.workshop.allowSandboxedAgents to expose skill_workshop to sandboxed agents (2 👍, needs-security-review). Link
  • #42475 — Per-agent cost budget enforcement at gateway (CLOSED but heavily discussed; likely to return). Link
  • #128067 — Field report bundling 6 reliability classes — effectively a roadmap signal for restart-recovery and persistence work. Link
  • #55372 — Config option to disable restart sentinel notification. Link
  • #138561 — active-memory plugin stops recalling after 2026.8.2 with no info-level signal (regression). Link

Prediction: Given the volume of memory-subsystem issues (#153426, #137613, #138561, #128140, #114913, #138366), the next releases are likely to prioritize memory provenance diagnostics, dreaming configuration, and memory-search deadline bounding over pure feature additions.

7. User Feedback Summary

Real user pain points visible in today's data:

  • Silent failure is the top complaint pattern. Memory files vanish (#153426), Slack DMs drop (#131150), tool parameters disappear (#53408), iMessage duplicates arrive (#143632), and WebChat duplicates text (#140723) — all with no user-visible error. Users repeatedly request diagnostics and recovery paths.
  • Operators want cost and resource control. #42475 (budget caps) and #67413 (dreaming OOM) show production deployments struggling with runaway spend and memory.
  • Multi-account / multi-agent deployments are stressed. #131150 (19 Slack accounts), #128067 (6 agents, heavy cron) — real-world scale exposes restart-recovery and identity-stability defects.
  • Mobile and voice UX remains friction-heavy. #137508 (Android keyboard occlusion), #124759 (iOS lag with reasoning panel), #164394 (WebChat jitter), #140455 (Meet voice), #138272 (Android Talk drops).
  • Upgrade safety is a recurring theme. #122019 asks openclaw update status to report plugin compatibility and irreversible-migration risk — indicating pain from 2026.9.x upgrades breaking plugin state (#167557, #144447).
  • Satisfaction signals: sustained high PR throughput from named contributors (vincentkoc, vyctorbrzezowski, roboclaw-bot, etzelm) shows an engaged community; UI phone-width PRs (#190387, #190372, #190409, #190420, #190432) demonstrate responsiveness to mobile feedback.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or aging high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  • #42475 — Per-agent cost budget (created 2026-03-10, CLOSED as stale after 29 comments). Users will re-file; needs product decision. Link
  • #53408 — Silent write/exec parameter drop (created 2026-03-24, still OPEN, 16 comments, needs-info). High user impact, low maintainer signal. Link
  • #91676 — skills.workshop.allowSandboxedAgents (created 2026-06-09, needs-security-review + needs-product-decision). Blocked on policy, not engineering. Link
  • #114913 — Memory-search embedding deadline bounding (created 2026-07-28, fix-shape-clear). Clear fix shape but no PR. Link
  • #128140 — memory_search 15s timeout vs. working CLI (created 2026-08-23, needs-live-repro). Link
  • #137613 — Pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends (created 2026-09-03, diamond lobster). Link
  • #141004 — feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage (open PR since 2026-09-07, XL size, no rating yet). Long-lived audit surface change. Link
  • #172274 — fix(browser): Chrome extension reports "Not installed" when macOS blocks profile reads (open since 2026-10-14, ready for maintainer look). Link
  • #180854 — fix(slack): stop replies after their parent is deleted (open since 2026-10-22). Link
  • #141932 — fix(agents): keep commentary line breaks in preamble progress text (open since 2026-09-08, marked stale despite proof: sufficient). Link

Maintainer attention priority: Items carrying both clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr and P0/P1 impact:crash-loop or impact:security flags (#160959, #153426, #187900, #167876) should be the first review targets — they are user-blocking, reproduce on current main, and have no code in flight.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Ecosystem Report — Personal AI Assistants & Agent Frameworks

Snapshot date: 2026-11-02 | Projects analyzed: OpenClaw (reference), Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape in late 2026 has consolidated around a gateway-plus-plugins runtime model, where a long-lived daemon brokers multi-channel messaging (Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Matrix, Feishu/Zalo), multi-surface clients (CLI, TUI, Desktop, WebUI, IDE/ACP), and pluggable memory/skill subsystems. All five projects in this snapshot are converging on the same architectural primitives — multiplexed gateway profiles, MCP tool interoperability, sandboxed execution, and persistent memory with provenance — but they diverge sharply in maturity, governance model, and community scale. The dominant engineering pressure across the ecosystem is no longer feature velocity; it is trust and operability: silent failures, cost runaway, session/identity ownership, and restart-recovery dominate the bug trackers. Two projects (OpenClaw, ZeroClaw) are in aggressive maturation with heavy review backlogs; one (Hermes) is consolidating a multi-profile stress point; one (QwenPaw) is bleeding-edge beta with active fixes in flight; and one (IronClaw) sits effectively maintenance-stalled on automated dependency traffic alone.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release Status Health Score* Trending
OpenClaw 500 updated (271 open / 229 closed) 500 updated (280 open / 220 merged-closed) No release today; latest 2026.10.8 62 / 100 Active, backlog-stressed
Hermes Agent 50 updated (48 open / 2 closed) 50 updated (41 open / 9 merged) No release 66 / 100 Stable, backlog-heavy
IronClaw 0 5 open (all Dependabot) No release 32 / 100 Stalled / maintenance-only
QwenPaw 4 updated (all open) 18 updated (17 open / 1 closed) No release; beta v2.3.0b2 58 / 100 Iterating on beta, merge-bound
ZeroClaw 9 updated (2 closed, 7 open) 48 updated (43 open / 5 merged) No release; target v0.9.0 70 / 100 High-velocity, review bottleneck

* Health score is a composite heuristic weighting: throughput vs. open-backlog ratio, presence of unaddressed P0/P1 blockers, merge cadence, and contributor diversity. Not an absolute measure — use for relative comparison only.

Observations:

  • OpenClaw is an order of magnitude larger than peers by raw throughput (500/500 vs. <60 for all others combined), but carries the largest absolute risk surface (multiple P0 crash-loop items with clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr).
  • ZeroClaw posts the best health composite: high contributor diversity, a clear security/identity roadmap, and same-day bug-fix turnaround (e.g., #12178 → #12179) — but only 5 merges against 43 open PRs.
  • Hermes has the healthiest merge review signals ([ci-reviewed] salvage PRs) but a 9:41 merge-to-open ratio.
  • QwenPaw is the only project with a public beta (v2.3.0b2) absorbing real breakage — a sign of active user adoption at the leading edge.
  • IronClaw is the outlier: zero human activity, a 71-day-old wasm dependency PR (#7834), and no issue engagement — effectively a project-in-hiatus signal.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale of community. 500 + 500 daily item updates versus 9–50 for every peer. Named contributor churn (vincentkoc, vyctorbrzezowski, roboclaw-bot, etzelm) is an order of magnitude denser than peers, who rely on a handful of prolific authors (ZeroClaw: Audacity88, Aarlington, IftekharUddin; Hermes: teknium1 + bot scaffolding).
  • Breadth of integrations. OpenClaw references Google Meet, iMessage, WhatsApp TTS, Zalo, Feishu, Slack, Matrix, Codex, Android Talk, macOS screen-record, and a plugin migration system — the widest channel/capability matrix in the snapshot.
  • Formal label taxonomy. P0 "diamond lobster," clawsweeper:*, impact:crash-loop, impact:security, provenance ratchets — a more mature (if backlog-stressed) triage apparatus than any peer.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw is architecturally a general-purpose agent runtime with gateway-level plugin generation and capture (the source of the #160959 event-loop regression), plus a curated-memory provenance system that peers lack.
  • It exposes openclaw doctor, openclaw update status, openclaw memory search — CLI diagnostics that Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw only partially match (hermes setup/hermes migrate are migration-centric; QwenPaw lacks a documented equivalent).
  • Cost governance is treated as a gateway-level concern (#42475), whereas ZeroClaw treats it at the daemon/channel layer and Hermes at the provider/credential-pool layer.

Community size comparison (relative):

Project Est. daily contributor surface Open backlog ratio
OpenClaw ~10× peer median 53% open
ZeroClaw ~3× median (concentrated) 90% open PRs
Hermes ~2× median (bot-assisted) 82% open PRs
QwenPaw ~1× median 94% open PRs
IronClaw bot-only N/A

Risk to OpenClaw's position: Its closure rate on high-severity bugs is the weakest relative signal in the snapshot — P0 items like #160959, #153426, #187900 carry no fix PR. This is precisely the gap peers (ZeroClaw, QwenPaw) are narrowing via same-day companion fixes and [ci-reviewed] salvage PRs.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Cross-project requirements emerging from independent community feedback:

A. Memory subsystem trust & provenance

  • OpenClaw: #153426 (curated MEMORY.md/USER.md silently excluded by provenance ratchet), #137613 (pre-compaction flush disabled on CLI), #138561, #128140, #114913.
  • Hermes: #132347 (holographic memory returns entire fact store), #127109 (FTS5 swallows all failures as "zero results"), #126181 (retrieval_count never incremented).
  • QwenPaw: #8500 (Auto-Dream silently drops a day of memory, checkpointed as success=True).
  • Need: Deterministic, diagnosable memory persistence with a relevance floor, error surfacing, and recovery paths.

B. Silent failures / observability gap

  • OpenClaw: #53408 (tool params dropped), #131150 (Slack DMs dropped), #141172 (leaked agent.run.started).
  • Hermes: #99270 (MCP array args corrupted), #146853 (Exa throttle as HTTP 200 success), #127109 (FTS5 silent zero).
  • QwenPaw: #8500 (silent memory drop with success report).
  • ZeroClaw: #12175 (personality editor copy lies about reload), #12176 (MCP HashMap ordering silently busts prompt cache).
  • Need: Every failure mode must be user-visible. This is the single most cross-cutting requirement in the snapshot.

C. Multi-profile / session identity isolation

  • Hermes: #145151, #135368, #147694 (UnscopedSecretError family under multiplex_profiles), #147600 (session.resume WebUI failures), #147071 (CLI detaches messaging channel).
  • OpenClaw: #167876 (Talk consultations lose caller authority), #138272 (Android Talk "no live response owner").
  • ZeroClaw: #12131 (shared execution permissions & credential renewal), #11286 (pairing-token-to-roster binding).
  • Need: Cryptographically enforced profile scoping, cross-surface session portability, orphan-safe credential rotation.

D. Cost & resource governance

  • OpenClaw: #42475 (per-agent gateway budget, closed-stale), #67413 (dreaming OOM).

7. Trend Signals

Industry trends extracted from cross-project community feedback, with implications for AI agent developers:

  1. Silent failure is the new top-priority UX defect class. Every project has ≥1 bug of the form "operation failed but UI reported success" (#8500 QwenPaw, #127109/#146853 Hermes, #12176 ZeroClaw, #53408/#153426 OpenClaw). Build for observability-first: every irreversible operation (memory write, message send, tool call) must have a surfaced failure channel.

  2. Memory is becoming a trust boundary, not a feature. Provenance ratchets (OpenClaw), relevance floors (Hermes #132347), and checkpoint integrity (QwenPaw #8500) converge on a single requirement: memory systems must be auditable and recoverable. Expect provenance metadata, retrieval diagnostics, and rollback APIs to become table stakes.

  3. Multi-tenancy forces identity/secret hygiene into the core. Hermes' UnscopedSecretError cluster and ZeroClaw's shared-execution-permissions RFC indicate that profile-scoped secret resolution and credential renewal without orphaned children will be required primitives, not options. Projects without profile isolation will fail at team scale.

  4. Cost and resource governance moves from policy to runtime. Three independent asks — gateway budget enforcement (OpenClaw #42475), non-restart cost override (ZeroClaw #11589), per-agent spend caps (Hermes #135816 cascade) — point to a runtime cost-controller becoming a first-class component, alongside per-agent memory/subprocess watchdogs.

  5. MCP is now infrastructure; interoperability correctness is a competitive differentiator. Hermes' most-commented bug is MCP array corruption; QwenPaw's top issue is MCP legacy handshake failure; ZeroClaw's is MCP ordering determinism. MCP conformance testing should be part of every agent project's CI.

  6. Multi-surface session ownership is unsolved across the ecosystem. CLI ↔ TUI ↔ WebUI ↔ Desktop ↔ messaging hand-offs break in OpenClaw (#138272), Hermes (#147071, #147600), and QwenPaw (#8033). The first project to ship a portable session-identity protocol (signed session tokens with surface-agnostic ownership) will gain a durable architectural moat.

  7. Merge-cadence — not feature velocity — is the emerging ecosystem bottleneck. ZeroClaw (5/48), QwenPaw (1/18), and Hermes (9/50) all show open-to-merged ratios that risk contributor attrition. For agent developers evaluating dependencies, merge-to-open ratio is now a more predictive health signal than release cadence.

  8. Platform-specific testing gaps are a universal liability. Windows argv quoting (Hermes #140831), TrueNAS Docker (Hermes #147612), fnOS sandboxes (QwenPaw #8515), and macOS Seatbelt regexes (ZeroClaw #12150) all surfaced as production blockers. Cross-platform CI matrices are underinvested across the entire ecosystem.

  • #8231 fix(console): persist market install provenance for 'Update All' — created 2026-10-13, marked Under Review; fixes #8176 and affects third-party plugin update coverage.
  • #8027 fix(skills): offload pool skill download to a worker thread — created 2026-09-29, a small blocking-I/O fix in an async handler; low-risk but unmerged for over a month.
  • #8367 conversation search and #8411 Matrix session recovery — both created in late October, sizeable and still open; early attention would prevent further drift.

Health note: The backlog skews toward fixes and rebases rather than feature creep, which is a positive sign — but the merge cadence (1 of 18 today) is the primary risk to both contributor retention and stability-issue turnaround. Prioritizing the three bug-fix PRs with linked issues (#8445, #8525, #8527) and unblocking the two oldest contributor PRs (#8178, #8170) would meaningfully improve project throughput.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows high-velocity development activity with 48 PRs and 9 issues updated in the last 24 hours, though only 5 PRs were merged/closed — indicating a substantial backlog of open reviews (43 open PRs). No new releases were cut. The project is in an intense maturation phase, with heavy focus on runtime durability, security/identity hardening, and channel reliability. Notably, the PR queue is dominated by large (size:XL) contributions from a small set of prolific authors (Audacity88, Aarlington, IftekharUddin), suggesting both strong contributor engagement and a potential maintainer review bottleneck. The absence of a merge/release cadence relative to the influx of new work is the primary health signal to watch.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. The most recent referenced release in the data is v0.9.0 (referenced in PR #11965 and issue #12154), suggesting v0.9.0 is either the current or imminent release target. No breaking changes or migration notes to report.

3. Project Progress

Only 5 PRs were merged/closed today (of 48 touched). Two issues were closed:

  • #12069 [CLOSED] — Feature request for /load-session <name|uuid> in ZeroCode's ACP pane to resume persisted sessions by name/UUID instead of relying on the Ctrl+S picker. Closing suggests acceptance/implementation.
  • #12154 [CLOSED] — Bug: install.sh printed the build commit v(99bd353) instead of the semantic version in the install summary. A quick, low-severity fix resolving user-facing install confusion.

Notable in-flight work advancing:

  • PR #12013 — regression test for TUI signing key precedence (extracted from #11422).
  • PR #12150 — fixes macOS Seatbelt sandbox regex that never matched ~/.cargo, ~/.nvm etc. (#12137).
  • PR #12179 — immediate companion fix to bug #12178 (deliver_file prose/uri confusion).

4. Community Hot Topics

Activity is heavily concentrated in a few high-touch threads:

  • Issue #9597 — "Make peer-agent turns durable and attributable" (3 comments, open since 2026-07-31, tagged risk:high, topic:agent-loop, follow-up). This is the longest-running active architectural discussion. The core need: peer-agent turns currently launch as detached process_message calls with no sender attribution or parent lifecycle, which undermines auditability and resource governance. This points to a deeper need for first-class task lineage in multi-agent orchestration.

  • Issue #12131 — RFC: Shared execution permissions & same-identity credential renewal (1 comment, type:rfc, security-triggered). Addresses a real multi-tenant scenario: a task receives input from several authenticated contributors and spawns children that outlive the initiating connection. The underlying need is safe credential rotation without orphaning or privilege escalation.

  • Issue #12130 — Configurable daemon session quotas with local operator reserve (1 comment). The daemon's hard-coded 64-session limit cannot distinguish dashboard/CLI/TUI/ACP connections, so a dashboard cap can starve operators. Clear demand for transport-aware capacity management.

  • PR #11589 — Operator override of exceeded cost limits (large, high-risk, spans every channel and the daemon). Currently, an exceeded shared cost limit can only be resolved by restarting the daemon — a significant operational pain point.

  • PR #11456 — Opt-in subprocess memory watchdog (open since 2026-10-02). Reflects demand for resource-safety guardrails on shell/skill subprocesses.

Pattern: The community's hottest discussions all revolve around governance and safety of autonomous execution — attribution, credentials, quotas, cost, and memory. This is a project whose users are pushing it from "personal assistant" toward multi-user, always-on infrastructure.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

Severity Issue Description Fix PR?
S2 #12176 Deferred MCP tool list emitted in HashMap order → system prompt changes every session → busts prompt caching (cost/perf regression) No
S2 (critical runtime) #12173 split_markdown_chunks in lark.rs slices at raw byte offset → panics when a byte budget lands inside a multi-byte UTF-8 char, taking down the channel task/daemon No
Low #12178 deliver_file description instructs model to write machine-only attachment:// uri into reply prose ✅ PR #12179
S3 #12175 Personality editor copy claims "no daemon reload needed" — false for channels, sends operators chasing phantom bugs No

Note: The Lark UTF-8 panic (#12173) is the most operationally serious new bug — a daemon-crashing panic from routine markdown chunking. It is unfixed. The MCP HashMap ordering bug (#12176) is a silent cost-cache regression with no fix yet.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Likely near-term (low-risk, scoped, or fix-aligned):

  • /load-session (from #12069, now closed → shipping).
  • deliver_file description correction (PR #12179).

Strong roadmap candidates for the next minor release:

  • Configurable daemon session quotas (#12130) — already has a placement RFC (PR #12132).
  • Operator cost-limit override (PR #11589) — documented-but-unimplemented config (cost.allow_override), likely to land given broad maintainer attention.
  • OIDC dashboard sign-in (PR #11965) and pairing-token-to-roster binding (PR #11286) — a security/identity cluster that could anchor a v0.9.x security release.
  • Telegram 429 flood gate (PR #11651) and Telegram rich messages (PR #11862) — channel maturity.

Longer-horizon: durable peer-agent turns (#9597) and shared execution permissions (#12131) are architectural and unlikely to land imminently.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points voiced by users:

  • Operational rigidity: Exceeded cost limits require a full daemon restart (#11589); hard-coded 64-session cap can't reserve operator capacity (#12130). Users are running ZeroClaw as always-on infrastructure and hitting fixed-limit walls.
  • Cost/caching regressions: Non-deterministic MCP tool ordering (#12176) and personality-file prompt churn (PR #11698) directly threaten prompt-cache efficiency — users are cost-sensitive.
  • Misleading UI/config: Personality editor copy (#12175) and deliver_file semantics (#12178) show a pattern of documentation/UI drifting from runtime truth, causing phantom debugging.
  • Reliability under load: The Lark panic (#12173) and Telegram 429 mishandling (#11651) indicate channel-edge robustness is a recurring concern.

Satisfaction signals: Rapid companion PRs (bug #12178 filed and fixed the same day by the same author) and maintainer acceptance of low-friction features suggest a responsive, contributor-friendly culture. No hostile or dissatisfied threads observed; feedback is constructive and engineering-focused.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention due to age, size, or risk:

  • Issue #9597 — open since 2026-07-31 (~3 months), risk:high, follow-up. Peer-agent durability is foundational but stalled; needs a decision/owner.
  • PR #11456 — open since 2026-10-02 (~1 month), size:XL, security:policy, ci:windows. Subprocess memory watchdog, broad blast radius.
  • PR #11355 — open since 2026-10-01, stale-candidate, WASM/Dioxus Skills dashboard PoC — appears to be waiting on a roadmap decision.
  • PR #10843 — open since 2026-09-13 (~7 weeks), stale-candidate, needs-author-action, large Telegram reaction fix.
  • PR #11286 — open since 2026-09-30, risk:high, security/pairing, distinguished contributor — strategic identity work aging in the queue.
  • PR #11589 — open since 2026-10-07, risk:high, touches every channel; high value but review-intensive.

Health assessment: ZeroClaw exhibits strong contributor momentum and a clearly articulated security/operations roadmap, but the growing gap between open PRs (43) and merge throughput (5/day) — combined with several high-risk PRs and a 3-month-old architectural issue — flags a review-capacity bottleneck that could delay the next release. Recommended focus: unblock the security/identity PR cluster (#11286, #11965) and land the crash fix for #12173.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-02

Generated: 2026-11-02 00:34 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Digest

Date: 2026-11-02 | Coverage: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI infrastructure stack is in a hardening phase rather than a feature-expansion phase: no project in this sample shipped a release in the last 24 hours, yet every tracker shows heavy issue/PR churn concentrated on correctness, memory accounting, and stability under concurrency. The day's most consistent cross-project theme is a DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 quality and stability gap — vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp each carry open bugs on DSV4-family correctness, scheduling, or backend crashes, indicating reference-implementation maturities have not yet caught up to model releases. Simultaneously, a Rust-ification of control planes is visible across layers (vLLM's Rust frontend, LiteLLM's Rust router core and forwarding server), targeting hot-path overhead rather than model math. Hardware coverage continues to broaden (SM100/SM120, ROCm gfx950, NPU, Hexagon, OpenCL/Adreno), but SM120 specifically emerges as a production risk across vLLM and SGLang. Finally, the training/fine-tuning layer (Unsloth) is extending parallelism and quantization reach (FP8 LoRA, unified DP/TP/PP/CP mesh), signaling that the same workloads serviced by inference engines are growing in scale upstream.

2. Activity Comparison

Note: exact counts are not published in the digests; the table reflects qualitative activity and explicit figures where cited.

Project Layer Active Issue Themes Active PR Themes Release Status (24h) Key Numerical Signals
vLLM Serving engine (server/cloud) ~8 ranked stability items; 3 engine-crash bugs Rust frontend parity; NVFP4/GPTQ batch-invariance; RL weight-reload RFC None RFC #54477 validated across 17 model families; ~18% pooling regression on torch 2.11; Rust roadmap #44280 at 50 comments
SGLang Serving engine (server/cloud) DSV4.1 crash + allocator OOM; SM120 GLM-5.3 issues SM100 NVFP4 kernels; AMD MI350X MiniMax; XPU paged-experts None Allocator OOM at only 29% KV pool; SM120 prefill 2–7K vs 12.5K tok/s vs vLLM/marlin; CUDA coredump tracker at 352 comments
llama.cpp Local/edge runtime SYCL multi-GPU cluster; CUDA sm_75 regression; Vulkan DSV4 gibberish Unified-KV FA; per-size CUDA graph arenas; MoE ClassLRU cache 6 releases (b12027–b12032) MoE ClassLRU: +6% QFN / +7% GLM decode, −8% uploads; SYCL --cpu-moe 100–1000× slowdown; HIP MTP prefill −80%
Ollama Local runtime + API surface Parser correctness (tool calls, harmony); long-context degradation Per-model prompt cache budgets; scheduler eviction; CORS hardening None Repeat-limit abort at 101 identical tokens; MLX cache fixed at 8 GiB; embed context off by 1–2 tokens
LiteLLM LLM gateway / proxy Cost/budget enforcement bugs; cross-tenant cache leak Large Rust router core migration (~10 stacked PRs); Rust forwarding server None Cost overbilling 1,000,000×; ~10+ Rust PRs in flight; GHCR tag/release provenance gap
Unsloth Fine-tuning / training Studio UX and platform fixes (mostly closed) FP8 LoRA; UNSLOTH_PARALLEL unified mesh; hub snapshot pinning None fp16 overflow example: B=5000 × alpha 16 = 80000 > 65504; Gemini picker capped at 20 models pre-fix

Reading: llama.cpp is the only project shipping releases, consistent with its continuous-build model. The server-grade engines (vLLM, SGLang) and control-plane layers (LiteLLM) are in deep refactor cycles, where regressions are expected and pinning discipline matters. Ollama and Unsloth are in bug-sweep mode.

3. Model Support Race

New model/architecture landings in this window:

Model / Arch vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 Batch-invariant sparse indexer (#64441); multi-image packing (#65030); HC expansion (#64816); MXFP8 indexer autotune (#60543) Bug-heavy: scheduler crash (#47218), allocator OOM (#43486), prompt-render divergence (#46348), SM120 index-order instability (#46798) Vulkan -fa on gibberish (#31480, fix PR #31505) — —
Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next Fused QK-norm+RoPE ROCm enablement (#51406) Qwen3.5 seq-classification request (#41110); GDN prefill + Triton recurrence (#38806) — 0.8B q4_K_M request (#19436) —
GLM-5.x Stale top-k fix (closed #63170) SM120 fa4 CUDA-graph crash (#42012) — triton only — — —
MiniMax-M3.1 NVFP4 KV sparse-prefill workspace (#64856) Landing: MI350X/MI355X gfx950 support (#46693, kernel stack merged) — — —
Mistral / Tekken developer→system role fix (#65031); byte-fallback tokenization fix (#64743) — — — —
Kimi K3 — NPU MLAProlog (#47373) — — —
LFM3 — — Tensor-split enabled (#31431) — —
Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe — — mtmd SALM support in review (#31471) — —
Gemma 4 — — Graph optimizations in review (#31356); test-arch enablement — —
Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid attn/MTP) — — — Support gap: GGUF load failure (#19459) —
Maple-Preview (TQ1_0/TQ2_0) — — CUDA kernels in review (#31512) — —

Who's ahead:

  • vLLM leads on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 depth — it is shipping optimizations for the architecture (sparse indexer, vision packing, MXFP8 autotune) while SGLang is still firefighting correctness and memory on the same model family.
  • SGLang leads on accelerator breadth — the only project landing MiniMax-M3.1 on AMD MI350X/MI355X and Kimi K3 on NPU in this window, plus an XPU paged-experts RFC. Its multi-vendor reach is a differentiator, at the cost of a wider bug surface.
  • llama.cpp leads on edge/mobile format breadth — Hexagon stride fix, OpenCL IQ3_S with Adreno kernels, ternary CUDA, LFM3 tensor split. This is the only project pushing into sub-server form factors.
  • Ollama lags on new-arch ingestion — Qwen3.8-27B hybrid-attention GGUFs still fail to load; harmony analysis-channel thinking support is the notable forward step.

4. Performance Frontier

Where optimization effort concentrates today:

Kernels (highest absolute effort)

  • SGLang: SM100 NVFP4 DualGEMM+SwiGLU, PDL-safe GEMM, grouped GEMM, fused MoE (#47589); single SM100-tuned RMSNorm JIT template (#47503); Qwen3 prefill QK-norm+RoPE fusion (#47785).
  • vLLM: ROCm FlyDSL decode monokernel (#63440); fused DSpark draft sampling on gfx950 (#63181); FlashInfer autotune expansion (#60543).
  • llama.cpp: OpenCL IQ3 Adreno GEMM/GEMV; unified-KV FA flash_attn_ext_rows (#29510) spanning CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/Metal/OpenCL/Hexagon/WebGPU.

KV / cache management

  • llama.cpp: unified-KV flash attention (mask-filtering elimination) and MoE ClassLRU expert cache (+6–7% decode, −8% uploads) — the most quantified cache win in the window.
  • Ollama: per-model prompt cache budgets (#19450) superseding a single global budget; scheduler eviction rework (#19449).
  • SGLang: NPU sparse-KV offload with PD disaggregation + LRU caching (#43579); supernode-wide L1/L2 agentic cache roadmap (#43098).

Quantization

  • FP4/FP8 dominance: NVFP4 across vLLM (KV, sparse indexer) and SGLang (dual-gemm, SM100, TP4 bundle).
  • Ternary/1-bit: llama.cpp OpenCL IQ3_S + Maple TQ1_0/TQ2_0 CUDA; vLLM BitNet request (#33142).
  • Training-side FP8: Unsloth FP8 LoRA on 16-bit bases (#16423).

Distributed serving / parallelism

  • Unsloth: UNSLOTH_PARALLEL unified DP/TP/PP/CP mesh (#16407) — the clearest training-scale parallelism advance.
  • SGLang: DSpark indexer-CP on NVFP4; TP4 NVFP4 serving bundle (#47807); Agentic Cache Scheduling roadmap.
  • vLLM: benchmarking RFC for reproducible BYO-GPU PR evals (#61698).

Batching / scheduling

  • llama.cpp: per-size CUDA graph arenas for small batches ≤8 tokens, avoiding speculative-verify recapture (#31156).
  • vLLM: batch-invariance work across NVFP4/GPTQ (correctness under batching, not just speed).
  • Ollama: fit-aware eviction at the 80% threshold.

Observation: The frontier has bifurcated. Cloud/server engines (vLLM, SGLang) are pushing 4-bit/FP4 kernels on the newest accelerator generations, while edge runtimes (llama.cpp) are pushing cache and graph-scheduling efficiency on format-varied hardware. The two rarely overlap, and a third track — distributed training parallelism — sits with Unsloth.

5. Layer Positioning

┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  APPLICATION / AGENT LAYER                                        │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  GATEWAY            │  LiteLLM — routing, budgets, cost tracking, │
│                     │  provider translation, virtual keys          │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  SERVING ENGINE     │  vLLM          │  SGLang                     │
│  (server/cloud)     │  throughput-   │  multi-vendor accelerators, │
│                     │  optimized,    │  broadest hardware reach,   │
│                     │  Rust frontend │  diffusion + LLM            │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LOCAL RUNTIME      │  Ollama        │  llama.cpp                  │
│                     │  UX-focused    │  lowest-level ggml/backend, │
│                     │  API wrapper   │  broadest quant + form      │
│                     │  over backends │  factor coverage            │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TRAINING /         │  Unsloth — LoRA/QLoRA/FP8 fine-tuning,      │
│  FINE-TUNING        │  parallelism mesh, Studio GUI               │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key differentiation:

  • vLLM and SGLang are direct competitors at the server engine layer. vLLM optimizes the reference-architecture path (DeepSeek-V4 depth, batch invariance, Rust frontend for hot-path overhead). SGLang pursues hardware breadth (AMD/NPU/XPU) and diffusion serving. Where they overlap (SM120, DSV4.1), they share the same bugs — suggesting common upstream dependencies (FlashInfer, Triton).
  • Ollama and llama.cpp are stack-adjacent, not competitors. Ollama is a user-facing runtime and API surface that consumes llama.cpp backends and MLX; its differentiators are scheduler policy, prompt caching, and API ergonomics. llama.cpp is the substrate — its innovations (unified KV, MoE cache, per-size graphs) propagate upward into Ollama and other consumers.
  • LiteLLM sits at the gateway layer, orthogonal to inference. Its Rust migration is about reducing proxy overhead, not model performance. Its critical risk profile is billing and multi-tenancy, not throughput.
  • Unsloth operates upstream of serving. Training outputs feed inference engines, and its FP8/parallelism work expands what can be fine-tuned — but it shares almost no operational concerns with the serving tier.

6. Trend Signals

Signal 1 — DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 is the ecosystem's stress test. Three of four inference projects carry open DSV4-family bugs, and vLLM's bug list (engine crashes, KV-connector failures, sparse-indexer divergence) mirrors SGLang's (scheduler crash, allocator OOM, prompt-render divergence). This is a maturity gap between model release cadence and engine support, not a single project's failure. Application developers should treat DSV4.1 serving as beta-grade through at least this quarter and pin verified builds.

Signal 2 — SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / Blackwell workstation) is not production-ready for frontier models. SGLang's fa4 CUDA-graph crash on GLM-5.3-Flash and its 2–7K vs 12.5K tok/s DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill gap, combined with vLLM's SM120 TurboQuant workspace bug and an open SM120 support request (#40802), indicate kernel coverage lags SM100 by roughly one release cycle. If you are evaluating RTX PRO 6000 for cost-efficient serving, budget for backend triage or wait for kernel roadmap items to land.

Signal 3 — Control planes are being rewritten in Rust. vLLM (frontend feature parity, 50 comments) and LiteLLM (router core, Redis client, forwarding server — ~10 stacked PRs) are both moving hot-path control logic to Rust, with byte-compatible Redis layouts to allow mixed-version rolling deploys. This is a coordinated pattern: Python orchestration on the edges, Rust on the request path. Operators should test dual-process topology changes (LiteLLM forwarding server) and Rust-frontend gating (VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1) in staging before enabling.

Signal 4 — Cost and budget enforcement in gateways is unreliable. LiteLLM's open 1,000,000× overbilling bug, team-member budget bypass via fallback, and crash on null token counts mean spend caps cannot be trusted as hard guardrails today. Combined with the cross-tenant exact-match cache leak (semantic caches scoped, exact-match not), gateway operators face both billing and isolation risk. Reconcile against provider invoices; disable exact-match caching across tenants; treat budget caps as best-effort.

Signal 5 — MoE expert caching is the practical VRAM-efficiency winner. llama.cpp's ClassLRU cache (+6–7% decode, −8% uploads) and Ollama's per-model cache budgets both target the same problem: serving large MoE models on constrained memory. If you run large MoE models locally or on mixed hardware, this is the highest-ROI optimization area in this window.

Signal 6 — Speculative decoding has backend-specific failure modes. llama.cpp's HIP --spec-type draft-mtp cuts prefill ~80%, while Vulkan is unaffected; Ollama's MLX runner aborts at 101 repeated tokens. Speculative decoding is not portable across backends — validate per-deployment rather than enabling globally.

Signal 7 — Multi-vendor accelerator support is widening, and with it, bug surface. SGLang is landing AMD MI350X/MI355X and NPU code paths; llama.cpp is adding Hexagon, OpenCL/Adreno, and XDNA requests; vLLM has open SM120/CPU-wheel/BitNet requests. The breadth is real, but non-NVIDIA paths consistently show stability and memory-accounting gaps (SYCL --fit under-accounts, 100–1000× --cpu-moe slowdown, DEVICE_LOST on tensor split). Multi-vendor deployments should expect a longer stabilization tail than NVIDIA-only fleets.

Signal 8 — Long-running RL/agent rollout loops are becoming a first-class design constraint. vLLM's direct-weight-reload RFC (#54477, validated across 17 model families), reset_prefix_cache() allocation-order request, and ID-only request-logging proposal (#64654) all point to the same workload shape: long-lived sessions where weight updates, prefix caching, and observability interact badly. SGLang's Agentic Cache Scheduling roadmap (#43098) addresses the same problem from the router side. Application developers building agent rollout infrastructure should design for cache invalidation and weight-reload semantics now, before these land.

What agent/application developers should watch:

  1. vLLM #54477 and #64654 — direct weight reload for RL and gateway-friendly request lifecycle logging.
  2. **SGLang

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24h, but activity is heavy on correctness and performance: a substantial RFC on direct weight reload for RL training (#54477) was revised after validation across 17 model families, batch-invariance work continues across NVFP4/GPTQ kernels, and a long-standing Rust frontend feature-parity roadmap (#44280, 50 comments) remains the most-discussed item. On the stability side, several engine-crash bugs are active: an async-scheduling preemption KeyError (#63549), a KV-connector load-failure crash on hybrid-KV models (#45474), and a Realtime ASR scheduler assertion (#35755).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None — no releases in the last 24h.

Adjacent developer-facing notes:

  • Tool-calling/offline examples: PR #55993 fixes "ghost demo.py" usage strings that referenced a nonexistent CLI in chat_with_tools_offline.py and the Mistral multimodal offline example — check your scripts if you copied from those examples. PR #55993
  • Quantization docs drift: the out-of-tree quantization plugin guide still references the removed FusedMoE class and an outdated MoE API. Issue #62187
  • --override-generation-config semantics: PR #45978 fixes special-token fields not being merged as documented. PR #45978

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Rust frontend: still experimental behind VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1; roadmap tracks Python-parity gaps. Issue #44280
  • DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1: batch-invariant sparse-indexer path (sorted top-k indices to avoid reduction-order divergence). PR #64441 · multi-image vision encoder packing via forward_packed. PR #65030
  • MiniMax-M3.1: reserve MSA Q8KV4 (NVFP4 KV) sparse prefill workspace during load so profiling accounts for it. PR #64856
  • Mistral: map developer role → system in MistralRenderer (fixes ValidationError under --tokenizer-mode mistral). PR #65031
  • Open requests: SM120 (RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000) support for DeepSeek-V4. Issue #40802 · prebuilt CPU-only wheels for basic testing. Issue #23096 · BitNet/ternary formats. Issue #33142

4. Performance & Optimization

  • ROCm / MI355X: FlyDSL decode monokernel for DSpark verify steps (--monokernel) persistent-launches decoder layers 1–60 across 1–16 requests. PR #63440 · fused DSpark draft sampling (markov GEMV + sample epilogue) on gfx950. PR #63181
  • Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5: enable the fused QK-norm+RoPE+gate Triton kernel on ROCm (currently CUDA-gated). PR #51406
  • DeepSeek-V4.1: vectorized first-layer HC expansion copy (Triton hc_expand). PR #64816 · FlashInfer autotune now covers the sparse indexer wq_b MXFP8 GEMM (previously never tuned). PR #60543
  • Regression watch: ~18% pooling throughput regression starting with torch 2.11 (vLLM v0.20.0+), reproduced on H100 PCIe. Issue #52630
  • Benchmarking infra: RFC proposes "Bring-Your-Own-GPU" reproducible evals/benchmarks attached to PRs to unblock perf/accuracy-sensitive reviews. Issue #61698

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity (engine-level failures first):

  1. Async scheduling + preemption crash — KeyError on all_token_ids[req_id] in Model Runner V1 _update_states; present on current main (c9dbc92). Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on Ascend 910B. Issue #63549
  2. Hybrid-KV KV-connector load failure kills EngineCore — _update_requests_with_invalid_blocks assumes a single KV cache group; hits DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Issue #45474
  3. Realtime ASR streaming — AsyncScheduler assertion (num_output_placeholders underflow) crashes EngineCore with /v1/realtime + Qwen3-ASR. Issue #35755
  4. MoE kernel import failure — _moe_C missing topk_softmax on Qwen3-30B-MoE (v0.10.0). Issue #22225
  5. TurboQuant long-context workspace — continuation prefill needs 12 MB vs 3.06 MB allocated beyond ~4096 tokens (Blackwell SM120, Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4). Issue #43357; related closed report #41565

If you're evaluating RTX PRO 6000 for cost-efficient serving, budget time for backend triage (triton works but is the fallback path) or wait for the kernel-coverage roadmap issues (#19637, #30272).

If you serve DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 through deepseek-recipe and see degraded tool-calling or reasoning quality, compare your token IDs against the checkpoint's own encoding.py (#46348). Prompt-rendering mismatches don't show up as errors.

llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-11-02

1. Today's Highlights

A burst of backend-specific fixes landed today: SYCL gained proper LevelZero discovery via PkgConfig (b12032), OpenCL picked up initial IQ3_S support including Adreno-tuned GEMM/GEMV paths (b12031), and Hexagon fixed a 24-bit DMA stride overflow that silently corrupted large-stride transfers (b12030). Meanwhile, the issue tracker is dominated by SYCL multi-GPU tensor-split problems — crashes, memory accounting gaps, and a new report of 100–1000× slowdowns with --cpu-moe — suggesting SYCL --split-mode tensor is not yet production-ready on Intel multi-Arc setups. On the PR side, the long-running unified-KV flash attention work (#29510) continues to attract attention, alongside new per-size CUDA graph arenas (#31156) targeting speculative decode.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No API-breaking changes or migration notes in today's release stream (b12027–b12032). Notable release-level content:

  • b12032 — SYCL: use PkgConfig for LevelZero includes/libs (#31076). Build-system improvement; packagers relying on hardcoded LevelZero paths should re-verify their toolchain.
  • b12031 — OpenCL: initial IQ3 support (#31338), with AOS/SOA mv kernels and a noshuffle GEMM/GEMV path for Adreno.
  • b12030 — Hexagon: fix DMA transfers with strides > 24 bits (#31442). Correctness fix for v75+ targets.
  • b12029 — mtmd: fix InternVL CLS token order (#30886). Vision-model users should upgrade if using InternVL.
  • b12028 — tests: enable Gemma 4 in test-llama-archs (#31401).
  • b12027 — llama: enable tensor split for LFM3 (#31431).

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • OpenCL / IQ3_S: first IQ3 quantization support on the OpenCL backend, including Adreno-specific kernels — relevant for Qualcomm mobile/edge inference. #31338
  • Hexagon (v75+): corrected DMA descriptor handling for strides exceeding 24 bits, unblocking large-stride tensor layouts on newer Hexagon DSPs. #31442
  • LFM3: tensor split now supported, enabling multi-GPU distribution of Liquid Foundation Models. #31431
  • Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (in review): mtmd support for NVIDIA's 30B-A4B SALM — offline transcription in 40 languages with prompt context and speaker attribution. #31471
  • Maple-Preview TQ1_0 / TQ2_0 on CUDA (in review): previously CPU-only ternary formats gaining CUDA kernels. #31512
  • Gemma 4 graph optimizations (in review): skips compute for layers not contributing to KV, with large prefill gains on E2B/E4B. #31356
  • XDNA backend request still open with strong community support (39 👍): #21725

4. Performance & Optimization

  • MoE expert cache — ClassLRU hybrid (#31233): replaces SLRU with a decaying-usage, class-ranked cache. Measured +6% decode on QFN, +7% on GLM, 8% fewer uploads with a warm cache. Directly relevant to anyone running large MoE models with limited VRAM.
  • Per-size CUDA graph arenas for small batches (#31156): separate graph results and schedulers for token counts ≤ 8, avoiding graph re-capture on speculative-verify size changes.
  • Unified KV cache flash attention (#29510): introduces flash_attn_ext_rows to avoid mask filtering overhead in multi-sequence inference — still in review, touches CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/Metal/OpenCL/Hexagon/WebGPU.
  • OpenCL IQ3 on Adreno (#31338): adds tiled matmul plus noshuffle GEMM/GEMV tuned for Adreno GPUs.
  • CUDA SWIGLU_CLAMP kernel (PR closed today) (#31517): implemented and validated for packed/strided/contiguous fp32/fp16 tensors.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. SYCL multi-GPU --cpu-moe is 100–1000× slower than single-GPU (#31510) — new today. 5-token prefill takes 165s on a 2× Arc Pro B60 host with all expert weights in host RAM. Severe if you're offloading MoE experts to CPU across multiple Intel GPUs.
  2. SYCL tensor split crashes with DEVICE_LOST (#27198) — 32 comments, long-running. Dual Arc Pro B70, crashes in dev2dev_memcpy despite working P2P.
  3. CUDA PTX toolchain regression on sm_75 (Tesla T4) (#31503) — server-cuda13 rolling images b11176/b11243/b12030 fail; b12004 works. Pin to b12004 or older if you're on T4.
  4. --spec-type draft-mtp cuts HIP prefill ~80% (#31495) — Vulkan unaffected. Avoid MTP speculative decoding on HIP until fixed.
  5. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash gibberish on Vulkan with -fa on (#31480) — a fix PR exists: probe the fused top-k mask with a graph that actually builds it (#31505).
  6. CUDA backend silently not registered in shared-library builds without GGML_BACKEND_DL (#31479) — no error, no warning, just missing CUDA0 in --list-devices.
  7. SYCL --fit under-accounts memory (#27595) — runtime overflow on Arc B70.
  8. Vulkan performance regression in recent builds (#24066) — oldest active regression, 49 comments, still open on RX 6600.
  9. MUL_MAT_ID MMVQ failure on Turing with mismatched arch targets (#30524).
  10. CUDA: Volta crash in FLASH_ATTN_EXT tests — fix PR open (#31518).

Also worth noting: M-RoPE batches read batch.pos past n_tokens (#28902), and update_slots() batch_view offset is not propagated to ctx_dft (#24840) — both subtle correctness issues affecting server-side batched inference.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin your CUDA builds if you're on Tesla T4 / sm_75. The b11176+ server-cuda13 images are broken; b12004 is the last known-good. Verify your container tag before upgrading.
  • Avoid SYCL tensor split in production for multi-Arc deployments. Both correctness (DEVICE_LOST) and performance (100–1000× regression with --cpu-moe) issues remain unresolved, and --fit memory accounting is unreliable. Single-GPU SYCL is fine.
  • MoE cache users should track #31233. The ClassLRU hybrid is a free 6–8% decode win with fewer expert uploads — meaningful if you're serving large MoE models on constrained VRAM.
  • Speculative decoding on HIP is currently a net loss for prefill-heavy workloads. If you rely on MTP draft models, route to Vulkan or disable --spec-type draft-mtp until #31495 is fixed.
  • Shared-library builders: if you set BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON and GGML_CUDA=ON but leave GGML_BACKEND_DL=OFF, CUDA will silently disappear. This is a footgun for custom embedding — check --list-devices in your CI smoke tests.
  • Server-side batched inference has two open correctness items (#24840, #28902). If you're building agents that rely on prefix caching or M-RoPE positional handling, keep an eye on these before relying on bit-exact replay semantics.
  • Unified KV cache + multi-sequence agents: the flash_attn_ext_rows work in #29510 is the one to watch — it directly targets the mask-filtering penalty that hurts concurrent agent workloads sharing a KV cache.

  • [OPEN] server: improve scheduler eviction selection (#19449, fixes #19326) — evaluates evictions against the pending request's predicted memory and GPU placement at the existing 80% fit threshold, and among equal keep-alive durations prefers the smallest idle runner that fits rather than blindly LRU-evicting. This is the highest-leverage throughput change in the queue: it should reduce unnecessary reloads under mixed-model load.

  • Guard your tool dispatch. #19425 can return a function name that doesn't match the argument object.
